jobs.descriptionHtml:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

Referrals are where care falls apart. A specialist referral leaves a primary care office as a fax, gets keyed into a queue by hand, waits on a phone call that nobody picks up, and lands back in an EHR days later with half the clinical context missing. Roughly a third never close the loop at all.

Orchestrator is the product that fixes this. It ingests referrals however they arrive (fax, phone, direct EHR feed), extracts the clinical and demographic data, handles the outbound coordination work that today eats a coordinator's entire day, and writes the result back into the EHR of record. It is a mix of document AI, voice automation, and hard integration engineering, sitting on top of a full-stack product that referral coordinators live in for eight hours a day.

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the team building it. This is an existing team with a shipping product and real customers, and you will grow it meaningfully over the next year. You will own delivery, drive the architecture decisions, and run your own hiring, working closely with the Director of Engineering on roadmap and prioritization. This is a good fit if you have a year or two of management under you, a deep engineering background, and you want the scope to grow quickly.

What You'll Do

  • Own delivery for Orchestrator end to end: intake pipeline, coordinator-facing application, voice automation, and EHR write-back.

  • Grow the team through hiring, and raise the technical bar as you do it. You will be running loops, closing candidates, and onboarding.

  • Stay technical. You will be in design docs, in code review, and on the occasional production incident. This is not a role where you stop reading diffs.

  • Set the integration strategy. Decide where we invest in durable interfaces (HL7 v2, FHIR, X12) versus where automation against the UI is the only option, and make those tradeoffs explicit.

  • Get the system ready for the next order of magnitude. Referral volume, customer count, and integration count are all growing, and the current architecture was built for the stage before this one.

  • Partner directly with existing customers, including the ones with the most complicated workflows. You will be on calls with health system IT, interface analysts, and clinical operations leads, translating between what they can support and what we need.

  • Turn those conversations into a generalized product. Every customer will describe their referral process as unique, and some of them will be right. Your job is to find the shared abstraction underneath, build that, and configure around the edges rather than forking the product per account.

  • Coach the engineers on your team into larger scope, and give direct feedback when scope is not being met.

What You Have

Required

  • Direct experience building software that integrates with EHRs. You have shipped and supported an integration against at least one major EHR platform, and can speak concretely about how it went wrong.

  • Working fluency in healthcare interoperability: HL7 v2 message structure, FHIR resources, and the operational reality of interface engines and site-specific customization.

  • Strong full-stack engineering background. You have built and operated production services and the interfaces on top of them, and you have opinions about both.

  • At least 1 year managing engineers, on top of 5 or more years as an IC engineer. We care more about the depth of the IC foundation than the length of the management track record.

  • Comfort with ambiguity in the problem space. Requirements here come from watching a coordinator work, not from a spec.

  • A track record of building products that serve many customers rather than one. You have said no to a well-funded one-off request, or said yes and then paid for it, and you can explain how you decide.

Nice to have

  • Experience with document AI or OCR pipelines at scale.

  • Experience with voice agents or telephony infrastructure (SIP, IVR navigation, real-time speech).

  • Background in referral management, prior authorization, care coordination, or revenue cycle.

  • Experience selling and supporting into large health systems, including security review and integration onboarding.

  • High-Value Deal Closure: Drive and close large deals ($1M+), while also identifying and capitalizing on land-and-expand opportunities within our growing enterprise visibility platform.

  • Exceed Quota: Proactively generate new business through your existing relationships, self-driven initiatives, inbound lead management, industry events, and strategic renewals and upsells.

  • Industry Expertise: Cultivate relationships with customers, decision-makers, and thought leaders, and stay abreast of new product developments and their potential market impact.

What You Have

  • Extensive Healthcare Sales Experience: 8+ years of experience selling into large healthcare systems, engaging with C-level executives (CNOs, CIOs, CTOs) and high-level operational leaders (VPs, Directors).

  • Sales Cycle Expert: Proven expertise in building pipelines, moving opportunities through complex sales cycles, and effectively presenting and discussing solutions with key decision-makers. You know how to "drive a deal.”

  • Passionate Evangelist: A highly energetic and driven individual with a strong sense of urgency and a deep belief in our mission.

  • Collaborative Team Player: Understanding of early-stage company dynamics and the importance of teamwork. You thrive in fast-paced, resource-constrained environments and embrace the "build-it-yourself" ethos.

  • Proven Track Record: Consistently achieved and exceeded revenue targets and sales goals.

  • SFDC Proficiency: Expert-level experience using Salesforce for forecasting, opportunity management, and reporting.

  • Consultative Sales Approach: Exceptional consultative sales skills, including the ability to define customer needs, qualify opportunities, present tailored solutions, and articulate business outcomes.

jobs.title: Senior iOS Engineer, Ambient AI
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We’re building a next-generation ambient AI platform for healthcare, helping clinicians focus on patient care by automatically capturing, understanding, and structuring clinical conversations in real time.

Mobile is at the center of this experience. Our apps support clinicians throughout their workflows, from capturing long-form conversations and reviewing AI-generated documentation to completing follow-up actions and coordinating care.

We’re hiring an iOS Engineer to help shape and build these experiences. You’ll own meaningful product areas from idea to launch, working closely with product, design, AI, and backend teams to turn emerging technology into intuitive, dependable mobile workflows.

This role is for an engineer who thinks deeply about the people using the product, not only whether a feature works, but whether it feels fast, clear, trustworthy, and natural in a clinical environment. You’ll spend most of your time building product experiences and owning the end to end delivery of these novel AI first workflows. Your work may also involve native mobile infrastructure challenges, and solving them to allow the product to scale.

Our mobile application is primarily built in Flutter, with native Swift/iOS integrations where platform-specific capabilities are required. Flutter experience is helpful but not required. We value strong mobile product judgment, native platform depth, and the ability to learn across the stack.

What You’ll Do

  • Build and own high-impact mobile experiences for clinicians, from early product exploration through launch, measurement, and iteration.

  • Develop new interaction patterns for AI-native healthcare software, including:

    • Real-time transcription and ambient documentation

    • AI-assisted review, editing, and clinical workflows

    • Multimodal inputs and intelligent recommendations

    • Agentic actions that help clinicians complete work

    • Offline and low-connectivity care experiences

  • Work closely with clinicians, product managers, and designers to understand real-world workflows and translate them into simple, thoughtful mobile experiences.

  • Partner with AI and backend engineers to bring model capabilities into production in ways that are responsive, understandable, and trustworthy.

  • Contribute across our Flutter application and its native Swift/iOS integrations.

  • Own the quality of what you ship, including performance, accessibility, reliability, analytics, testing, observability, and release readiness.

  • Prototype quickly, learn from real usage, and refine experiences based on qualitative and quantitative feedback.

  • Help shape mobile product and technical strategy as the Ambient AI product line grows.

  • Mentor other engineers and raise the bar for mobile engineering, product thinking, and craft across the team.

  • Occasionally contribute to adjacent surfaces such as our web application or Chrome extension when a workflow spans platforms.

What You Have

  • 4+ years of professional mobile development experience, with meaningful ownership of user-facing products or features.

  • Deep experience in iOS or cross-platform mobile development.

  • Strong native expertise in Swift/iOS, including platform conventions, app lifecycle, permissions, background execution, and performance.

  • Experience working in or a willingness to ramp onto a Flutter-based codebase.

  • A track record of taking mobile experiences from ambiguous ideas to polished, production-ready products.

  • Strong product judgment and attention to interaction details, usability, performance, and overall craft.

  • An understanding that reliability is part of the user experience, particularly for workflows involving recording, connectivity, background execution, or sensitive data.

  • Experience collaborating closely with product, design, backend, data, or AI teams.

  • Comfort moving between product features and the underlying mobile systems required to support them.

  • An ownership mindset and bias for action. You identify important problems, create clarity, and drive work through completion.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience building AI-native, conversational, or real-time product experiences.

  • Experience with audio or video capture, streaming, transcription, or background recording.

  • Experience with offline-first applications, sync engines, resilient local persistence, or conflict handling.

  • Flutter and Dart experience, including Riverpod or similar state-management patterns.

  • Experience designing or contributing to mobile design systems and reusable component libraries.

  • Familiarity with mobile experimentation, product analytics, and measuring feature adoption or usability.

  • Experience improving startup time, responsiveness, memory usage, battery consumption, or crash rates.

  • Experience with mobile observability, CI/CD, testing, release automation, or App Store and Play Store workflows.

  • Exposure to healthcare, HIPAA, SOC 2, privacy, security, or other regulated environments.

  • Light JavaScript, TypeScript, Chrome extension, or web application experience.

Why Join

  • Build a product that directly gives clinicians more time to focus on their patients.

  • Create new mobile interaction patterns at the intersection of AI, healthcare, and real-world clinical workflows.

  • Work across the full product lifecycle, from understanding user problems to shipping and improving the experience.

  • Solve distinctive mobile challenges involving real-time audio, offline behavior, multimodal AI, and agentic workflows.

  • Have meaningful influence over mobile product direction, technical architecture, and engineering culture.

  • Join at a stage where individual engineers can shape both what we build and how we build it.

  • Grow into broader mobile product or technical leadership as the team and product expand.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Data Warehouse
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer to own Commure's data warehouse platform end-to-end. You'll design, build, and operate every layer of the stack:

  • CDC pipelines

  • Streaming transport

  • Schema governance and data contracts

  • Query and serving layer

  • Analytics platform

The core stack today: Debezium for CDC, StarRocks as our MPP query and serving engine, and dbt for transformation and modeling. This is a hands-on IC role with broad scope. You'll make architectural calls, write the code that matters most, and set the patterns other teams build on.

What You'll Do

  • Own the data warehouse platform end-to-end: CDC pipelines, data lake, query layer, transformation layer, and the analytics-facing tooling that sits on top.

  • Design and operate CDC pipelines with Debezium (and Kafka, Redpanda, or an equivalent streaming backbone) that move data from operational databases into the warehouse with low latency and high fidelity.

  • Architect the data lake on object storage using an open table format (Iceberg, Delta Lake, or Hudi) with Parquet, enabling both batch and streaming workloads and clean separation of storage from compute.

  • Run and scale StarRocks (or adjacent MPP/lakehouse engines) as the query and serving layer - schema design, materialized views, ingestion patterns, tuning, and cost/performance trade-offs.

  • Build the transformation layer with dbt: modeling standards, tests, documentation, and a semantic layer that gives every team a single source of truth for metrics.

  • Stand up orchestration (Airflow, Dagster, or similar) and the CI/CD, observability, and data-quality tooling that make the platform trustworthy day-to-day.

  • Partner with Security and Compliance on PHI/PII handling, access controls, lineage, and auditability so the platform meets HIPAA and SOC 2 bar by default.

  • Set patterns and conventions: schema contracts, ingestion patterns, and self-serve tooling - that let product and analytics teams build on the platform without needing you in the loop for every decision.

What You Have

  • 6+ years of software engineering experience, with significant time building or operating data platforms at scale.

  • Experience across the modern data stack: CDC (Debezium or equivalent), streaming (Kafka, Redpanda), data lake formats (Iceberg, Delta, Hudi), an MPP or lakehouse query engine (StarRocks, ClickHouse, Trino, Snowflake, Databricks), and dbt.

  • Fluent in SQL, schema design, query optimization, and reasoning about cost and latency trade-offs on large datasets.

  • Experience running production data infrastructure (orchestration, observability, on-call, data quality, and incident response).

Preferred

  • Direct experience with Debezium, StarRocks, and dbt in production.

  • Experience building semantic layers (dbt Semantic Layer, Cube) or data catalogs / lineage (DataHub, OpenMetadata, Amundsen).

  • Experience with HIPAA-regulated data (PHI handling, de-identification, and access governance).

  • Experience powering AI/ML workloads: feature stores, training-set curation, embedding pipelines, or retrieval systems.

  • Experience across multiple clouds (AWS, GCP, Azure), infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi) and Kubernetes controllers.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join Air Billing, the team behind the highest-traffic surfaces in our practice management product: claims, appointments, and payments posting — the workspaces billers and practice staff live in all day.

These aren't basic CRUD screens. They're fast, data-dense, keyboard-driven workflows over millions of claims, sitting on real healthcare plumbing (EDI transactions, payer automations). AI is central to how we drive productivity, but we don't solve everything with an agent — we put LLMs in the loop only where day-to-day friction is highest.

We're mid-way through a generational rebuild of these surfaces, and there's an enormous amount to build: rebuilding the claims workspace, making bulk operations safe over tens of thousands of records, stitching together a unified claim activity timeline, and putting AI to work where billers feel the most friction. As a Senior Software Engineer, you'll own end-to-end features across this work and see them run in production for billers every day.

You'll join a small, tight-knit team that owns the claims, appointments, and eligibility surfaces end-to-end. It's a hands-on group that ships fast, reviews each other's work closely, and sits right next to the billing operators who use what we build — so you'll see the impact of your features in days, not quarters.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Own features end-to-end on the claims, appointments, and payments-posting surfaces — from design phase through production rollout

  • Write production-ready code with meaningful tests and observability, and design clean interfaces and data models that hold up as the surfaces grow

  • Partner with product, design, and billing operations to make sure what you ship actually solves the biller's workflow problem

  • Build reliability and observability into your features — dashboards, logging, and alerting that make production issues fast to catch and root-cause

  • Review code and designs with an eye toward correctness, performance on data-dense screens, and a consistent user experience

  • Help set the technical standards and direction the team builds on as we scale — shaping component patterns, API and data-fetching conventions, and testing and observability practices, and helping onboard and level up teammates

 

What You Have

  • 5+ years building full-stack applications, with a track record of shipping features end-to-end in production

  • Solid frontend skills — you build clean, maintainable UIs and can diagnose and fix common rendering issues in data-dense screens

  • API and data-layer fundamentals — you can build backend endpoints handling filtering and pagination over sizable datasets, and reason about the queries behind them

  • Sound technical judgment for feature-level work — you evaluate tradeoffs, escalate risks appropriately, and avoid over-engineering

  • Good debugging and observability instincts — comfortable with monitoring, logging, and alerting

  • Clear communication — you keep teammates and partners informed, and ask questions early when things are unclear

  • Ownership mindset and bias for action — you take responsibility for your features and follow through with urgency and customer focus

 

Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with healthcare billing data — EDI X12 (270/271, 276/277, 835, 837), clearinghouses, ERAs/EOBs, denial codes — or a demonstrated ability to ramp on a gnarly domain quickly

  • Experience shipping LLM-powered features into production workflows, not just demos

  • Exposure to analytical/OLAP stores alongside a transactional database

  • Strong product intuition and a track record of influencing UX/UI decisions to improve usability

  • Experience working in regulated industries (healthcare, finance, insurance) with attention to security and compliance

jobs.title: Request for Proposal Manager (India)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role
We are looking for highly organized RFP & Proposal Managers to help our sales team develop high-quality responses to Requests for Proposal (RFPs), Requests for Information (RFIs), and related customer questionnaires.


This is a hands-on role for someone who can independently manage the complete proposal process—from reviewing requirements and coordinating with internal teams to drafting, editing, and submitting a compelling final response. The ideal candidate understands enterprise sales, writes clearly, manages deadlines rigorously, and can work across multiple stakeholders with minimal supervision.

What You’ll Do

  • Own RFPs, RFIs, proposals, and customer questionnaires from initial review through final submission.

  • Review requirements, identify mandatory criteria, and create a clear response plan.

  • Partner with sales leaders to understand the opportunity, customer priorities, competitive landscape, and win strategy.

  • Coordinate inputs from product, engineering, security, legal, finance, implementation, and other subject-matter experts.

  • Draft clear, persuasive, and customer-specific responses rather than relying solely on generic content.

  • Manage timelines, assignments, reviews, approvals, and submission requirements.

  • Ensure every response is accurate, complete, consistent, and aligned with the customer’s evaluation criteria.

  • Identify missing information and proactively follow up with the appropriate stakeholders.

  • Edit technical and business content for clarity, tone, grammar, and consistency.

  • Prepare executive summaries, company profiles, solution descriptions, case studies, and implementation narratives.

  • Maintain an organized library of approved answers, supporting documents, templates, and reusable content.

  • Track open proposals, deadlines, outcomes, and common reasons for wins and losses.

  • Improve the RFP process by introducing effective templates, workflows, and quality-control practices.

  • Manage multiple time-sensitive proposals without compromising quality.

What You Have

  • Experience in proposal management, RFP responses, bid management, sales enablement, presales, enterprise sales, or a related role.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage complex, deadline-driven projects.

  • Excellent written English, editing, and business communication skills.

  • Strong understanding of B2B or enterprise sales processes.

  • Ability to translate technical or complex information into clear, persuasive customer-facing language.

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to follow complex submission instructions.

  • Experience collaborating with sales teams and cross-functional subject-matter experts.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Google Workspace, and common collaboration tools.

  • Sound judgment and the confidence to challenge incomplete, unclear, or weak responses.

  • Ability to prioritize effectively and remain composed under tight deadlines.

Nice to Have

  • Experience responding to enterprise, government, or regulated-industry RFPs.

  • Familiarity with proposal-management or RFP automation platforms.

  • Experience with security questionnaires, due-diligence requests, and procurement processes.

  • Knowledge of structured proposal methodologies or formal bid-management practices.

  • Experience building and maintaining an RFP content library.

  • Familiarity with CRM systems and sales pipeline management.

Please be aware that all official communication from us will come exclusively from email addresses ending in @commure.com. Any emails from other domains are not affiliated with our organization.


Employees will act in accordance with the organization’s information security policies, to include but not limited to protecting assets from unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, destruction or interference nor execute particular security processes or activities. Employees will report to the information security office any confirmed or potential events or other risks to the organization. Employees will be required to attest to these requirements upon hire and on an annual basis.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer on the Network Infrastructure team to own the networking backbone of our multi-cloud, application, and corporate infrastructure that every other engineering team at Commure relies on. This is a horizontal team supporting multi-product infrastructure, and the network layer is yours to design, build, and operate end-to-end:

  • Multi-cloud network foundation and IaC

  • Hybrid and on-prem connectivity

  • Kubernetes and service networking

  • Edge, load balancing, and DNS

  • Network security and zero-trust access

  • Network observability

  • Network automation using GitOps

The stack today runs on public cloud (GCP, AWS, and Azure), with all infrastructure defined as code (Terraform and controller-based). Argo CD drives deployment; Helm handles application packaging; Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry power observability. Networking is an active build-out toward cloud-native patterns (Kubernetes-native networking, eBPF, Gateway API, service mesh), and the shape of it is yours to define.

This is a hands-on IC role with broad scope. You'll make architectural calls, write the code that matters most, and set the patterns other teams build on.

What You'll Do

You'll own several of these verticals within the team's scope end-to-end.

  • Own the multi-cloud network foundation: VPC design, routing, transit hubs, IPAM and IPv6, and multi-region failover across GCP, AWS, and Azure. Managed as code with Terraform and Crossplane

  • Build hybrid and on-prem connectivity: IPsec VPN, BGP, Cloud Interconnect / Direct Connect / ExpressRoute, and traffic engineering for data centers, regional hubs, and remote offices

  • Design the Kubernetes networking layer: CNI (Cilium, eBPF), ingress via Gateway API and Envoy, Istio (or equivalent) service mesh, and mTLS

  • Run the edge: load balancing, DNS, WAF, DDoS mitigation, and rate limiting

  • Secure the network by default: firewalls, segmentation, zero-trust access, and encryption in transit. Partner with Security on policy-as-code that meets HIPAA and SOC 2

  • Own network observability: flow logs, packet capture, and eBPF visibility (Hubble), wired into OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, and Grafana

  • Treat the network as code: GitOps with Argo CD, pre-merge validation, and self-serve modules for product teams

  • Debug the hard problems: TCP/UDP, NAT, connection tracking, asymmetric routing, MTU, and kernel networking

What You Have

  • 6+ years of experience in cloud native networking or infrastructure engineering

  • Deep expertise in network fundamentals: TCP/UDP/ICMP, BGP, IPsec, NAT, stateful firewalls, VLANs, bridges, TUN/TAP, and connection tracking

  • Experience with public cloud networking (GCP, AWS, Azure)

  • Experience with Kubernetes and cloud-native networking (CNI, eBPF, Gateway API, Envoy, Istio)

  • Experience with Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, Pulumi)

  • Experience designing and operating VPN and site-to-site connectivity at scale

  • Experience with BGP route filtering, multi-path routing, and traffic engineering

  • Experience with network security: firewalls, WAF, DDoS mitigation, segmentation, and zero-trust

  • Experience with network observability and performance troubleshooting (flow logs, packet analysis, latency, packet loss)

Preferred

  • Experience with Cloud Interconnect (Dedicated Interconnect, Direct Connect, ExpressRoute)

  • Experience with kernel network tuning and BGP route optimization

  • Experience running DNS infrastructure at scale

  • Experience with on-prem or hybrid environments and data center networking

  • Contributions to CNCF networking projects (Cilium, Envoy, Istio)

  • Experience with network automation and testing (GitOps, Batfish, containerlab)

  • Experience in regulated industries with HIPAA, SOC 2, or PCI obligations

You don't need to check every box: strong network fundamentals, cloud native or Kubernetes background matter most.

Please be aware that all official communication from us will come exclusively from email addresses ending in @commure.com. Any emails from other domains are not affiliated with our organization.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We are looking for a driven, highly communicative, and data-oriented Sales Development Representative (SDR) to join our team in India, supporting our US Sales team and US customer base.

As an Sales Development Representative, you will be responsible for building and running the outbound systems that identify potential customers, research relevant decision-makers, reach out through cold email and LinkedIn, and help build a qualified sales pipeline. This is a digital-only role with no cold calling.

This is a high-impact, target-driven role where your ability to build automated workflows, work with data, research prospects, write compelling outreach, learn quickly, and continuously improve what works will directly contribute to our sales growth.

What You'll Do

  • Research and map target accounts: Build a deep understanding of target organizations, including their structure, leadership, technology footprint, financial state, and current initiatives. Map the buying committee at each account and identify the right people to approach, in what order, and how to handle their likely objections.

  • Build prospecting systems: Create automated workflows using Clay, APIs, and AI to identify, enrich, verify, and prioritize ideal-fit accounts and decision-makers across a large named-account portfolio.

  • Prioritize with data: Score and tier accounts by fit and buying signals, so high-priority accounts get deep personalization and the rest get an efficient, still-relevant approach.

  • Build a messaging system: Create a persona library and reusable templates that stay specific to each account and person, rather than reading like a mail merge.

  • Run and optimize email campaigns: Plan and execute cold email campaigns end to end, from list segmentation and sequence design to copywriting, A/B testing, and send scheduling. Monitor open, reply, and bounce rates, and continuously refine targeting and messaging to increase qualified replies and meetings booked.

  • Run LinkedIn outreach: Engage prospects on LinkedIn alongside email through connection requests, messages, and genuine engagement with their content, using AI-assisted personalization that still reads like a human wrote it.

  • Manage email deliverability: Set up and maintain cold email sending infrastructure, including secondary domains, mailboxes, warm-up, and authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), working with IT and compliance on approvals. Monitor bounce rates, inbox placement, and sender reputation to keep deliverability strong as volume grows.

  • Monitor buying signals: Set up automated tracking of triggers such as leadership changes, job postings, vendor announcements, and financial results, and use them to adjust account priority and messaging.

  • Automate the manual work: Build internal tools and automations, such as reply classifiers, alerts, and research workflows, using tools like Claude Code, OpenAI API, n8n/Zapier, and Slack.

  • Qualify and hand off: Handle replies quickly during US business hours, qualify interest, and book meetings for US Account Executives with a clear account brief and accurate Salesforce records.

  • Measure and improve: Track the funnel from first touch to qualified opportunity. Run experiments on targeting, messaging, and timing, and scale what works.

  • Work across teams: Coordinate with marketing, AEs, and leadership on support beyond email and LinkedIn, such as ABM ads, events, and executive outreach. Share what you learn from the market with sales, marketing, and product.

What You Have

  • 1–3 years of hands-on experience in outbound, growth, or GTM roles with a track record of booking meetings with B2B decision-makers (US market preferred)

  • Proven experience running cold email and LinkedIn campaigns, including sequence design, A/B testing, sending infrastructure and deliverability, and staying within LinkedIn’s usage limits

  • Practical experience with Clay and at least one sales engagement tool (Outreach, Smartlead, Instantly, Apollo, or similar)

  • A builder’s mindset: you’ve shipped working automations or internal tools using AI coding tools, APIs, webhooks, or no-code platforms, and you know how to check AI output for accuracy before it reaches a prospect. You don’t need to be a software engineer, but you need to be comfortable building.

  • Strong research skills: you can turn public information into a sharp, accurate account brief and a reason to reach out now

  • Strong written English. You can write outreach that senior executives actually read, and clear prompts for AI tools.

  • Strong business writing and presentation skills: you can turn research and analysis into clear documents and slide decks that stand on their own

  • Comfort with data: cleaning, segmenting, and reasoning about thousands of records, and doing the funnel and capacity math to plan your work

  • Ownership of results, comfort with targets, and the ability to work US business hours

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Scribe AI
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We're a small, fast-moving team with ambitious growth goals. We're looking for innovative Full Stack Engineers who can ship quickly and help bring new solutions to market. As we scale, you'll also raise the bar, evolving our engineering practices and setting the standard for how we build.

This full-time position requires working 5 days a week in our Mountain View, CA office, with occasional travel to meet customers.

What You'll Do

  • Develop and scale features for our AI medical scribe, using cutting-edge LLM models to create accurate, structured clinical notes.

  • Build polished, responsive user experiences across our web and iOS applications.

  • Build and maintain robust infrastructure for audio processing, cloud services, and integrations with enterprise EHR systems.

  • Lead projects from zero to one in a fast-paced environment, working closely with product and design teams.

  • Work directly with customers: join calls, gather feedback, and turn it into product improvements quickly.

  • Collaborate closely with designers, product managers, and external stakeholders.

What You Have

  • [Required] Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent extensive experience

  • 1–4 years of professional software development experience. Strong new grads who can show they pick up new technologies quickly are encouraged to apply.

  • Strong experience in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and modern frameworks (React, Next.js, Node.js/Express), plus iOS development with Swift and/or React Native.

  • Experience with development for both web and mobile, specifically iOS

  • You stay calm under pressure and do well in a fast-paced, customer-facing environment.

Please be aware that all official communication from us will come exclusively from email addresses ending in @commure.com. Any emails from other domains are not affiliated with our organization.


Employees will act in accordance with the organization’s information security policies, to include but not limited to protecting assets from unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, destruction or interference nor execute particular security processes or activities. Employees will report to the information security office any confirmed or potential events or other risks to the organization. Employees will be required to attest to these requirements upon hire and on an annual basis.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Voice Agents
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

Health system call centers can't keep up with patient demand. 85% of patients who can't get through never call back. They go elsewhere, and appointments that should have been booked never are.

We're building AI Voice Agents that pick up every call and handle the full conversation: scheduling, rescheduling, cancellations, confirmations, FAQs, and intake. They work by integrating directly with the EHR and telephony stack in real time.

We're hiring a Software Engineer to build the systems these agents run on: the voice pipelines, EHR integrations, and services that take a call from "hello" to a booked appointment. It's a mid-level role on a small team that ships every day, with a lot of room to grow into harder problems.

This full-time position requires working 5 days a week in our Mountain View, CA office.

What You'll Do

  • Design and build backend services in Python that power real-time voice agents: call orchestration, conversation state, tool execution, and EHR write-back.

  • Architect low-latency pipelines connecting telephony, ASR, LLMs, and TTS into a single conversational loop.

  • Lead integrations with healthcare systems (like Epic, Cerner, athena, and others) for scheduling, eligibility, and intake.

  • Drive design decisions on APIs, data models, and event-driven workflows, and mentor other engineers on the team.

  • Partner with AI, product, and operations to ship features patient access teams actually use.

  • Set the bar for what ships: latency, reliability, observability, and release readiness.

What You Have

  • 4+ years of backend software experience, primarily in Python.

  • A track record of designing and shipping production services, APIs, and data models that others build on.

  • An intuition for how people interact with automated assistants through voice and text, where the rules are different than icons and buttons.

  • Deep experience with async, event-driven, or real-time systems.

  • Strong fundamentals in testing, LLM evaluation, observability, and reliability.

  • A patient-centered mindset. You design for the person on the other end of the line, not just the metrics.

  • Bias for action, an ownership mindset, and the judgment to know when to move fast and when to slow down.

Please be aware that all official communication from us will come exclusively from email addresses ending in @commure.com. Any emails from other domains are not affiliated with our organization.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, AI Accounting & Ledger Systems
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We're hiring a Senior Engineering Manager for the team that owns the financial core of our revenue cycle product. That's three things: the ledger that records every financial event, the reports that billing managers and CFOs close their books on, and the analytics that tell a practice how it's doing.

You'll manage 6 to 8 engineers, from early-career to Senior Staff, own the roadmap with your product partner, and be accountable for financial correctness across the platform. We're partway through rebuilding this surface: moving a decade of report logic onto a drift-free ledger and a modern OLAP layer, while customers keep closing their books on the old one.

What You'll Do

  • Manage and grow a team of 6 to 8 engineers. Hiring, performance, career growth. Build people who can each run a customer escalation, a data migration, or an incident end-to-end without you in the room.

  • Set the roadmap with your product partner. The goal is to get from building whatever report a customer asked for to customers building their own reports and closing their books without us involved.

  • Own financial correctness. For this team, wrong numbers are a worse failure than a slow page. You'll own the systems that catch silent errors: shadow parity harnesses, cross-report tie-out checks, drift monitoring, and correctness SLOs next to the uptime ones.

  • Lead multi-quarter migrations (ledger report migration, OLAP golden views) incrementally, with parity checks at each step, without breaking anyone's close.

  • Own the customer relationship at the top of the stack. Sit with comptrollers, CFOs, and RCM directors at our largest sites during month-end. Turn their definition of "correct" into software, and turn recurring escalations into roadmap.

  • Run cross-team execution with the payments/posting team, data infrastructure, and ops so upstream changes don't quietly break downstream numbers.

What You Have

  • 5+ years managing software engineers, including senior and staff-level ICs. You've grown engineers into leads and staff engineers, and you can name them.

  • You've shipped financial, reporting, or data-intensive systems in production where the numbers had to tie. You know how a report can be technically correct and still wrong to the person reading it.

  • Backend and data fluency. You can review a query plan, push back on a ledger design, and debug a parity failure yourself. Staff engineers will take you seriously because you engage with the substance.

  • You've set direction for a product surface and can say what it should look like in 12 months.

  • You're comfortable across the table from a CFO explaining why a number moved.

  • Operational discipline: on-call, SLOs, and monitoring for correctness as well as availability.

  • You move fast on incomplete information and reset timelines honestly when the work turns out bigger than expected.

Nice to Have

  • Healthcare RCM, billing, practice management, or clearinghouse background. Or fintech experience with ledgers, close automation, or reconciliation (BlackLine, FloQast, Numeric, Stripe, Modern Treasury).

  • OLAP stores (StarRocks, ClickHouse, Druid) run alongside PostgreSQL.

  • Double-entry accounting, append-only ledgers, or audit-trail requirements.

  • Leading a platform re-architecture while keeping the existing system shipping.

  • Shipping LLM features to production. We run an AI report builder that handles thousands of custom reporting requests.

Please be aware that all official communication from us will come exclusively from email addresses ending in @commure.com. Any emails from other domains are not affiliated with our organization.

Employees will report to the information security office any confirmed or potential events or other risks to the organization. Employees will be required to attest to these requirements upon hire and on an annual basis.

About the Role:

You will lead Commure’s Sales Development team and own the pipeline it produces for our enterprise sales organization. You will coach SDRs, build the outbound motion with sales leadership, and decide which accounts, segments, and channels get the team’s time. Our GTM motion is still taking shape, so you will set how the team prospects, qualify opportunities, and hand them off, then adjust as results come in.

What You'll Do

  • Manage, coach, and develop a team of SDRs through weekly 1:1s, call reviews, and live pipeline inspection

  • Own the team’s pipeline and meeting targets, and report on progress to Sales and Marketing leadership

  • Build and refine outbound campaigns into health systems, hospitals, and physician groups with Sales, Marketing, and RevOps

  • Set the account prioritization framework, using intent data and community intelligence tools to point the team at high-intent prospects

  • Define qualification criteria and the SDR-to-AE handoff, and hold both sides to it

  • Run experiments across channels (calls, email, social, events, warm intros) and keep what works

  • Hire, onboard, and ramp new SDRs, including training on Commure’s products and how to talk with health system leaders

  • Document playbooks, talk tracks, and best practices so new reps ramp faster

  • Manage tooling and data hygiene across CRM, sequencing, and enrichment platforms

  • Join senior-level conversations with prospects when a deal needs it

What You Have

  • 7+ years of experience in sales development, with at least 3–5 years managing SDRs or BDRs (or a strong record as a team lead moving into management)

  • A record of building and scaling outbound pipeline, with results you can quantify

  • Experience coaching reps to consistent, repeatable performance over multiple quarters

  • Fluency in outbound tooling: Salesforce, a sequencing platform, intent data, and enrichment tools

  • Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to speak credibly to health system executives

  • A data-driven approach to funnel analysis, with the ability to spot where conversion drops and fix it

  • Interest in AI and in using it to make your team more efficient

  • Comfort in an unstructured environment where you build the process as you go

  • Experience selling into healthcare or health IT is a plus

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We’re building a next-generation ambient AI product suite for healthcare, helping clinicians focus on patient care by automatically capturing, understanding, and structuring clinical conversations.

Behind that experience is a distributed system responsible for ingesting long-form audio, processing real-time and asynchronous streams, orchestrating multiple AI models, and reliably producing clinical outputs. These workflows must remain observable and recoverable across network interruptions, partial failures, model timeouts, and rapidly changing inference infrastructure.

We’re hiring a Staff Backend Engineer to help build and operate this foundation. You’ll work across audio ingestion, media processing, inference orchestration, distributed workflows, storage, observability, and cloud infrastructure.

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys making complex systems dependable. You think carefully about failure modes, idempotency, backpressure, data integrity, latency, and operational simplicity. You also understand that infrastructure exists to serve the product: the systems you build must ultimately create a fast, reliable, and trustworthy experience for clinicians.

What You’ll Do

  • Design, build, and operate backend systems that power our Ambient AI products across mobile and web.

  • Build and evolve inference workflows that coordinate transcription, diarization, language models, clinical extraction, summarization, and other AI capabilities.

  • Develop orchestration systems for long-running, multi-stage workflows, including:

    • Scheduling, queueing, and workload prioritization

    • Retries, timeouts, fallbacks, and dead-letter handling

    • Idempotency, replay, and safe workflow recovery

    • Model routing, versioning, and configuration

    • Progress tracking and user-visible workflow state

    • Graceful degradation when dependencies are unavailable

  • Improve the reliability and scalability of services operating under variable, compute-intensive workloads.

  • Define and maintain service-level objectives for critical workflows, including availability, processing latency, completion rates, and data durability.

  • Build strong observability across services and pipelines through structured logging, metrics, distributed tracing, dashboards, alerting, and diagnostic tooling.

  • Lead incident response and post-incident analysis for important production failures, turning operational lessons into lasting improvements.

  • Identify systemic failure patterns and eliminate them through better abstractions, automation, testing, and architecture.

  • Improve cloud infrastructure, deployment systems, capacity planning, and operational tooling as the platform scales.

  • Design APIs and data models that allow mobile, web, and internal systems to interact with long-running workflows safely and predictably.

  • Build tools that make inference pipelines easier to inspect, test, replay, evaluate, and debug.

  • Balance reliability, latency, quality, and infrastructure cost across AI and media-processing workloads.

  • Partner closely with mobile, product, AI, security, and clinical teams to turn new capabilities into production-ready workflows.

  • Mentor other engineers and help establish strong practices for distributed systems, observability, operational readiness, and backend architecture.

What You Have

  • 8+ years of professional backend or infrastructure engineering experience.

  • Experience designing, building, and operating production distributed systems.

  • Strong proficiency in at least one modern backend programming language.

  • Experience with asynchronous processing, message queues, event-driven systems, or durable workflow execution.

  • A strong understanding of distributed-systems concepts such as idempotency, consistency, concurrency, backpressure, retries, failure isolation, and eventual completion.

  • Experience operating services in a cloud environment, including deployment, monitoring, scaling, and incident response.

  • Experience designing APIs, service boundaries, and data models for complex product workflows.

  • A track record of improving system reliability, observability, scalability, or operational efficiency.

  • Strong debugging skills across application, infrastructure, data, and external dependency boundaries.

  • An ability to reason about both real-time and long-running workloads with different latency and durability requirements.

  • Comfort working across backend, infrastructure, product, and AI systems rather than within a narrowly defined layer.

  • An ownership mindset and bias for action. You identify important risks, create clarity, and drive ambiguous infrastructure work through completion.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience building speech-to-text, diarization, transcription, or other audio-based machine-learning workflows.

  • Experience orchestrating large language models or multi-model inference pipelines in production.

  • Familiarity with workflow orchestration systems such as Temporal or similar durable execution platforms.

  • Experience with event-streaming and messaging technologies such as Kafka, Pub/Sub, SQS, or similar systems.

  • Experience with model routing, inference gateways, rate limiting, batching, caching, or GPU-backed workloads.

  • Experience building internal tooling for workflow inspection, replay, evaluation, or model debugging.

  • Experience defining SLOs, managing error budgets, designing alerts, and leading production incident response.

  • Familiarity with distributed tracing and observability platforms such as Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Sentry, or similar tools.

  • Experience with containers, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, and cloud-native deployment systems.

  • Experience optimizing systems for throughput, tail latency, infrastructure cost, and workload isolation.

  • Experience with offline clients, background synchronization, or systems that reconcile delayed and duplicated events.

  • Exposure to healthcare, HIPAA, SOC 2, encryption, privacy, security, or other regulated environments.

  • Experience supporting AI-native, real-time, or agentic product experiences.

Why Join

  • Build the backend foundation for an AI healthcare product used in real clinical workflows.

  • Solve challenging systems problems involving distributed orchestration, and production AI.

  • Make reliability improvements that clinicians experience directly through faster, safer, and more dependable workflows.

  • Shape how inference systems are orchestrated, observed, recovered, and scaled in production.

  • Work closely with product and AI teams while maintaining deep ownership of backend architecture and infrastructure.

  • Help define the operational and engineering standards for a rapidly growing platform.

  • Join at a stage where core systems, technical strategy, and engineering culture are still highly shapeable.

  • Grow into broader backend, infrastructure, or technical leadership as the team and product expand.

Please be aware that all official communication from us will come exclusively from email addresses ending in @commure.com. Any emails from other domains are not affiliated with our organization.


Employees will act in accordance with the organization’s information security policies, to include but not limited to protecting assets from unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, destruction or interference nor execute particular security processes or activities. Employees will report to the information security office any confirmed or potential events or other risks to the organization. Employees will be required to attest to these requirements upon hire and on an annual basis.

About the Role

The Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) Product Team at Commure + Athelas powers the core operating system for our practices. Our product—Insights—provides practice staff and administrators with everything they need to efficiently manage their practice’s operations. We maintain 150+ customer-facing features, ranging from high-level reports and visualizations to workflow automation tools to help the staff boost their practice’s revenue.

As a Senior Software Engineer Engineer, you will play a key role in scaling and maintaining our website’s infrastructure, ensuring a seamless user experience as we grow to support thousands of practices nationwide.

Beyond development, this role will help define the technical direction of Insights’ architecture, shaping how and where services are built and deployed. You’ll help foster a culture of continuous improvement, enhancing the reliability, scalability, and performance of our web applications while elevating the technical skills of the entire engineering organization.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Drive the technical direction of our practice management platform, Insights, ensuring it scales to support thousands of practices and millions of users

  • Design, build, and maintain scalable full-stack solutions using ReactJS, Python, and PostgreSQL

  • Improve system reliability and observability by implementing best practices in monitoring, logging, and alerting

  • Optimize performance and scalability of our web applications, ensuring seamless user experiences as we rapidly expand

  • Collaborate with infrastructure and backend teams to ensure high availability and resilience of core functions

  • Mentor and guide engineers, fostering a culture of technical excellence and continuous learning

  • Lead and deliver high-impact projects, balancing speed and quality in a fast-paced, high-ownership environment

  • Conduct in-depth code reviews, uphold best practices, and drive architectural improvements across the stack

  • Work closely with product and design teams to build intuitive, user-friendly experiences for healthcare providers and staff

 

What You Have

  • 5+ years of professional software development experience, with a focus on building scalable full-stack applications

  • Proficiency in full-stack development with expertise in JavaScript (React/Vue), Python, and PostgreSQL

  • Strong architectural skills with experience designing and maintaining highly scalable, reliable, and performant web applications

  • Experience leading multi-month, high-impact projects, balancing trade-offs, and delivering results in a fast-paced environment

  • Deep understanding of modern front-end engineering—React fundamentals, performance optimization, state management, and component-driven design

  • Experience working with complex backend systems, including designing APIs and optimizing database performance

  • Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, with a focus on observability (monitoring, logging, and alerting best practices)

  • Ability to mentor engineers and drive technical excellence across the organization

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to effectively present technical concepts to leadership and cross-functional teams

 

Nice to Have

  • Experience scaling front-end applications in a fast-growing, high-traffic environment

  • Deep understanding of frontend performance optimizations and ability to diagnose bottlenecks in React applications

  • Strong product intuition with a track record of influencing UX/UI decisions to improve usability

  • Background in data visualization and building interactive dashboards for analytics-heavy applications

  • Experience with developer tooling and CI/CD pipelines for frontend applications

  • Familiarity with modern API design patterns (GraphQL, REST, gRPC) and best practices in backend-for-frontend (BFF) architectures

  • Contributions to open-source projects or a strong engineering blog presence

  • Experience working in highly regulated industries (finance, insurance, government) with a focus on security and compliance

  • A passion for improving healthcare and healthcare operations in America

About the Role

Commure's finance team is rebuilding revenue accounting from the ground up, and this role is the architect of that rebuild. We're creating a brand-new Manager, Revenue Accounting & Deal Operations position to do two things at once: stand up our deal desk function from scratch, and modernize the technical infrastructure that supports revenue recognition across a fast-growing, multi-product healthcare technology business.

This isn't a maintain-the-status-quo role. Building the process, the playbooks, and the cross-functional muscle memory with Sales, Legal, and Revenue Operations that doesn't yet exist at scale. What You’ll Do

Revenue Accounting Transformation & Technical Accounting-

Modernize revenue accounting processes: Transform the revenue accounting lifecycle, from contract review through revenue recognition, with a focus on scalability, automation, and IPO-ready internal controls.

Lead technical accounting assessments: Research complex accounting matters and prepare technical accounting memos under ASC 606, covering multi-element arrangements, complex contracts, and non-standard deal structures.

Develop and maintain accounting policies: Establish, maintain, and enhance revenue recognition policies to ensure consistent application across an expanding and diversifying product portfolio.

Technology & Automation-

Drive technology adoption: Evaluate and implement revenue automation solutions and AI-enabled finance tools to reduce manual effort, and revenue accounting workflows, and improve accuracy and efficiency.

Operational Revenue Accounting

Support monthly and quarterly close: Collaborate on revenue close activities, including account reconciliations, journal entries, deferred revenue analysis, and account-level reviews, ensuring timely and accurate financial reporting.

Strengthen financial controls: Support external audits and develop scalable, SOX-compliant processes that promote accuracy, consistency, and audit readiness.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner with FP&A: Support revenue forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis by providing accurate, well-documented accounting inputs and clear explanations of revenue trends.

Compliance & Audit-

Support external financial audits: Prepare schedules and supporting documentation requested by auditors (PBC schedules), respond to revenue-related inquiries, and ensure audit requirements are met accurately and on time.

Drive IPO readiness: Strengthen revenue recognition policies, process documentation, and internal controls to align with public-company reporting and compliance expectations.

What You Have-

  1. 6+ years of progressive accounting experience, including at least 3 years of hands-on experience specifically in Revenue Recognition, Revenue Accounting, or Technical Accounting within a high-growth or complex business environment.

  2. Strong expertise in US GAAP and ASC 606, with the ability to independently interpret and apply revenue recognition guidance to complex accounting scenarios.

  3. Proven experience reviewing and assessing complex customer contracts, including multi-element arrangements, non-standard commercial terms, contract modifications, variable consideration, and performance obligations to determine appropriate revenue recognition treatment.

  4. Hands-on experience managing revenue accounting activities, including contract assessments, revenue recognition analysis, deferred revenue, journal entries, account reconciliations, and month-end or quarter-end close.

  5. Experience preparing technical accounting memos, documenting accounting judgments, and establishing consistent revenue recognition policies and procedures.

  6. Bachelor's degree in accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA or CA preferred.

  7. Hands-on experience with NetSuite, Salesforce, and revenue automation tools, with an interest in AI-enabled finance technology.

  8. Experience supporting external financial audits and developing or maintaining SOX-compliant processes and internal controls.

  9. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with exceptional attention to detail.

  10. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex accounting matters to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

  11. Ability to manage multiple priorities, take ownership of ambiguous situations, and drive process improvements in a fast-paced, scaling private-company environment.

  12. Experience working with US-based businesses, customers, or Finance teams and applying US GAAP in a US-market business environment is highly desirable.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the role

We're hiring a hands-on Head of Performance Creative to own the creative engine behind our paid growth. On Meta today, creative is the targeting: the platform decides who sees an ad by reading the ad itself, and the accounts that win are the ones feeding it the most distinct, customer-true concepts. You will be the person who makes that happen.

This is not a brand or content-calendar role, and it is not an agency-management role. You will listen to customer and sales calls, pull out the pains and the words clinics use, turn them into concepts, produce the ads yourself with AI tools and a small bench of creators, read what the account tells you, and feed the next round. Much of our analysis and reporting is already automated. Your job is the judgment, the customer insight and the output that automation cannot produce.

You'll report to the VP of Growth Operations and work directly with Sales, RevOps and Product. You'll own the creative pipeline for our paid accounts end to end, with a clear path to building a team as the engine proves out. The number you own is qualified pipeline per dollar of creative spend, not clicks and not raw leads.

What you'll do

  • Mine customer insight. Live in our customer and sales call recordings, support tickets and onboarding notes. Keep a current map of pains, objections and proof points by buyer: practice owner, clinic director, front desk, biller. Keep a library of verbatim quotes we are cleared to use.

  • Own creative strategy. Turn that insight into a steady stream of structurally distinct concepts, each with a new angle, buyer or format, not a headline swap. Give each a hypothesis and a kill metric. Run a modular testing system underneath: once a concept wins, swap hooks, openers, calls to action and formats to find its ceiling. Decide what enters testing each week and what graduates to scaling.

  • Make the ads. Produce statics and short video yourself with AI generation, editing and voice tools. Start from what we already have: hours of customer and sales calls, customer testimonial recordings, founder clips and product captures. Write the hooks and the scripts, cut the footage or brief an editor, and ship finished ads, not briefs. Target in the first 90 days: six or more new concepts into testing every week.

  • Build the creator bench. Recruit, brief and direct clinicians, practice owners and UGC creators for testimonial and founder-style content. Own consent, releases and claims compliance for everything that runs.

  • Launch and QA your own ads. Build and launch inside Meta Ads Manager: naming conventions, primary text, headlines, placements, UTMs. Check every placement render before it goes live. A test that launches with a broken link or the wrong form is a wasted week.

  • Read the data yourself. Work in the ad account and our dashboard without an analyst: hook rate, hold rate, cost per qualified lead by concept and audience, cohort reads that account for a multi-week sales cycle. Separate creative effects from audience effects. Kill fast.

  • Build with AI as a system. Prompt libraries, generation pipelines, agents that score tests and surface quotes. Improve the workflows we already run and build the ones we don't have. Catch what the AI gets wrong before it ships.

  • Extend beyond Meta. Carry the message past the click. Keep ad copy, landing pages, forms and the first SDR touch telling the same story, and work with Sales and RevOps when they drift. Repurpose winning concepts into LinkedIn, YouTube and Google as those channels open.

What you have

  • 5+ years in performance creative or creative strategy for paid social, with a portfolio of ads you made and concepts that scaled to meaningful spend.

  • Hands-on creative and ad-account experience across major paid channels, including Meta, Google, YouTube, LinkedIn and TikTok. You know how each platform works in practice: account structure, launch mechanics, testing cadence, creative formats, optimization signals, and what a winning concept looks like on each.

  • You've made the content yourself: scripts, statics, short video that drove direct-response results. Briefing others is not enough.

  • Working SQL. You can pull your own lead-level and creative-level data, join ad results to CRM outcomes, and read an ad account without an analyst. You're comfortable when results land weeks later and samples are small.

  • Daily, systematic use of AI across research, writing, image and video. You can show the workflows and say what you tried and dropped.

  • A customer-insight habit. You'd rather listen to a call than read a persona document.

  • You've run a high-volume creative pipeline: footage libraries, creator briefs, editing queues, launch checklists. Nothing slips because you lost track of it.

  • You've worked directly with customers or creators to make content, and you can direct someone on camera.

  • A bias toward shipping. When something doesn't exist, you make it.

Nice to have

  • Built and run a creator or UGC pool: recruiting, briefing, rates, releases.

  • B2B SaaS, healthcare, or selling to small businesses and clinics.

  • Python or a notebook habit for analysis beyond SQL.

Who you are
