The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

You'll own partnerships that bring Commure's AI into more healthcare organizations and extend its technology, data, and content capabilities. Your portfolio will span major EHR vendors; independent software vendors (ISVs); data, technology, content, and embed partners; systems integrators (SIs); resellers; and group purchasing organizations (GPOs).

Your mandate is to turn partnerships into revenue and new capabilities. Some will build repeatable pipeline; others will drive 0-to-1 transformation, opening new markets, bringing new products to life, and repositioning Commure in the market. Often the same partner will do both. You'll own each partnership from first conversation to live deployment.

You'll start as a hands-on builder, owning partnerships directly and shaping how the function grows. You'll report to the Chief Strategy Officer, one of the founders at Commure, who reports directly to the CEO. You'll have autonomy and company-wide visibility, working across sales, product, engineering, operations, customer success, marketing, legal, and finance.

This role is onsite up to 3 days per week at our Mountain View office, San Francisco office, or both, as specified by Commure.

Anticipated travel is 10%–25% of working time for partner visits, user groups, conferences, and joint customer meetings.

What You'll Do

  • EHR Alliance Management: Own relationships with major EHR vendors, including executive engagement, joint application programming interface (API) and integration priorities, implementation capacity, and escalations. Align product and engineering commitments with deal and deployment priorities.

  • Partner-Sourced Pipeline: Drive partner-sourced pipeline and revenue across enterprise and mid-market accounts, with opportunities across Commure's business units. Act as the partner sponsor on deals, coordinating partner support with sales and customer success through live deployment.

  • Channel, SI, and Reseller Development: Build channel, systems integrator, and reseller partnerships with signed agreements, account coverage plans, and joint sales execution. Define enablement plans, lead ownership, and commercial terms with sales, legal, and finance. Extend the model to GPOs, with legal review of referral and payment terms before launch.

  • Strategic and Capability Partnerships: Find the ISV, data, technology, content, and Powered by Commure embed partners that expand what Commure can do and where it can compete. Vet each against customer demand and our engineering, implementation, and legal capacity. Then work with sales, product, engineering, legal, and finance to set integration scope, usage rights, and launch criteria before committing.

  • Partner Events: Build account and meeting plans for EHR user group meetings, industry conferences, and other priority partner events. Work with sales and marketing to turn meetings into qualified opportunities with clear owners and follow-up plans.

  • Performance and Operating Cadence: Track sourced and assisted pipeline separately, along with conversion, revenue, and live deployments. Maintain the partner lead tracker and give Commure leadership weekly updates on deal stages, partnership activity, blockers, and next actions.

What You Have

  • Relevant Experience: 4–8 years of total professional experience, including building software-as-a-service (SaaS) or technology partnerships, whether your path ran through channel and alliance sales or through consulting, investment banking, or corporate development. We also welcome product managers and engineers with substantial partnership experience. Healthcare or digital health experience is a plus but not required.

  • Relationship Building: Ability to earn trust with senior executives and turn relationships into active partnerships.

  • Executive Communication: Ability to develop models and briefings and deliver compelling product presentations to C-suite executives, boards of directors, and other audiences, virtually and in person.

  • Technical Fluency: Ability to engage fluently with internal and partner teams on technical topics, including high-level architecture diagrams, APIs, and joint integration plans.

  • Contracting: Ability to review contracts in depth and co-draft business terms with legal while maintaining strong attention to detail.

  • AI-Native Workflow: A passion for helping healthcare providers embrace AI and interest in using approved AI tools in your own work, from supporting contract review with legal to developing presentations, interpreting technical diagrams, and managing dashboards and key performance indicator (KPI) reporting.

  • Strategic Judgment: A point of view on where Commure should partner, build, or wait, grounded in a strong read of the healthcare technology and AI landscape (or the curiosity to build one fast). You're comfortable with ambiguity and know how to turn an early partnership idea into a new product, channel, or market.

Please be aware that all official communication from us will come exclusively from email addresses ending in @commure.com. Any emails from other domains are not affiliated with our organization.

Employees will report to the information security office any confirmed or potential events or other risks to the organization. Employees will be required to attest to these requirements upon hire and on an annual basis.

At Commure, we are building technology to simplify healthcare for patients, providers, and administrators. We're looking for a Senior Manager of Demand Generation to turn our account fit and intent data into campaigns that generate enterprise pipeline, both from new accounts and from expansion within our existing customer base. This person will own B2B paid media, campaigns, campaign operations, the lead lifecycle, and funnel measurement for our enterprise portfolio, including Ambient AI, Call Center Agents, and Orchestrator, and report directly to the Head of Enterprise Marketing.

This is a senior, high-impact role for an AI-first marketer with deep B2B paid media experience who can turn Commure's brand narrative into paid programs that build awareness and pipeline with enterprise healthcare buyers. You'll be equally comfortable building a HubSpot workflow, writing a campaign brief that rallies the team, and presenting results to sales leadership. You'll use AI to move faster than a traditional demand gen function, and you'll help the rest of the team do the same.

What You'll Do

Paid Media and Brand Narrative

  • Own Commure's enterprise paid media strategy, budget, and channel mix across LinkedIn, Google, ABM, and programmatic, with spend tied to pipeline and revenue targets

  • Partner with brand and content to turn our positioning into paid creative, offers, and multi-touch storylines that tell Commure's story consistently to health system and enterprise buyers

  • Run account-based paid programs against our fit and intent model, coordinated with SDR outreach and sales plays

  • Direct agency and platform partners, and test creative, audience, and offer to improve cost per opportunity and pipeline per dollar

  • Report paid performance on pipeline, account engagement, and brand lift so leadership can see how spend builds both demand and awareness

Campaigns and Programs

  • Build and run integrated campaigns and account plays against our fit and intent model, prioritizing the accounts most likely to convert

  • Partner with Customer Success to build expansion campaigns that drive cross-sell and upsell across our existing customers

  • Lead each campaign end to end with a clear brief and timeline, bringing content, brand, web, social, events, and sales along from kickoff to results readout

  • Own the webinar calendar and direct mail programs

Campaign Operations

  • Partner with our Events Manager on the pre-show and post-show motion, including attendee list enrichment, list loading, and follow-up plays

  • Set up and manage campaigns in HubSpot and Salesforce so every touch is tracked and attributable

Lead Lifecycle and Nurture

  • Optimize lead and account scoring, lifecycle stages, and routing logic, partnering with Revenue Operations on implementation

  • Build email nurture series and design the handoffs between marketing nurture, sales nurture, and SDR follow-up

Measurement and Optimization

  • Own lead and opportunity attribution and report on funnel performance from first touch through closed-won, for both new business and expansion

  • Test, measure, and optimize conversion at every stage, and turn results into clear recommendations

Sales and SDR Alignment

  • Partner with the SDR team on scripting, sequences, and activity plans so follow-up matches each campaign

  • Train sales and SDR teams on campaigns and lead handling, and hold teams to agreed follow-up SLAs

AI and Marketing Technology

  • Serve as marketing's expert HubSpot power user, working with Revenue Operations to expand what our stack can do

  • Use AI to accelerate research, enrichment, segmentation, personalization, reporting, and campaign builds, and help the team adopt AI workflows that save time

What You Have

  • 7+ years in B2B demand generation, including 3+ years owning paid media programs and budgets

  • Hands-on expertise running B2B paid programs across LinkedIn Ads, Google Ads, and ABM or programmatic platforms such as 6sense or Demandbase, including audience strategy, creative testing, and budget pacing

  • A portfolio of paid campaigns that carried a brand narrative to enterprise buyers and moved both awareness and pipeline

  • Hands-on expertise in HubSpot or a similar marketing automation platform, plus Salesforce

  • Proven experience using AI to build or scale marketing workflows

  • A track record of scoring, nurture, and ABM programs that drove measurable pipeline

  • Strong project management, writing, and presentation skills

  • Healthcare experience is a bonus

About the Role

We're hiring a senior Growth leader to architect and operate our growth engine from the ground up — hands‑on. This isn't a "manage the agency" role. You'll be the one designing the system, wiring the stack, running the experiments, and shipping the assets. You think in funnels and frameworks, build measurement infrastructure before you launch campaigns, and treat go-to-market as an engineering discipline: instrument, test, iterate, scale.

You'll work directly with Sales, RevOps, Product, and Brand to turn signal into pipeline — and you'll be the one who actually builds the things that make that happen. Critically, you'll own the number: net new business in the form of marketing qualified leads is your north star, and you'll be accountable for hitting it. This will be a high-visibility role with incredible growth opportunities.

 

What You'll Do

Ad Engine Ownership & Performance Marketing

  • Own the design, build, and continuous optimization of our ad engine across paid search, paid social, programmatic, and video — with a focus on efficiency, scale, and measurable pipeline contribution.

  • Architect audience segmentation, bidding strategies, creative rotation logic, and budget allocation frameworks to maximize return on ad spend.

  • Move beyond channel management: treat the ad engine as a product, iterating on targeting logic, landing page pairings, offer variants, and conversion pathways to compound performance over time.

  • Own hands‑on execution — you're in the platforms, not just reviewing reports.

Driving Net New Business: MQL Ownership

  • Own the MQL number. You are directly accountable for generating net new marketing qualified leads that convert into pipeline and revenue.

  • Build and operate the demand generation engine that fills the top of funnel — from first touch to sales-ready hand‑off — with clear SLAs, routing logic, and feedback loops.

  • Define and enforce MQL quality standards in partnership with Sales and RevOps, continuously tightening the criteria as signal improves.

  • Report on MQL volume, velocity, cost-per-MQL, and downstream conversion rates; use those inputs to direct investment across channels and programs.

Scaling the Marketing Foundation: 1 to 100

  • Take the marketing foundations already in place — brand narrative, positioning, early channel presence, initial playbooks — and build the operational engine that scales them.

  • Translate strategy into a repeatable growth system: standardized processes, campaign architecture, channel playbooks, and asset libraries that multiply output without multiplying headcount.

  • Identify what's working at small scale and build the infrastructure — tooling, measurement, creative, ops — to run it at 10x without losing fidelity or efficiency.

  • Close the gaps between brand and demand: ensure every scaled program reinforces positioning while driving measurable business outcomes.

Full-Funnel Growth System Ownership

  • Design and own the full‑funnel growth architecture: paid (search, social, programmatic, video), organic (SEO, content, web), ABM, partnerships, and referral.

  • Build the experimentation infrastructure — test frameworks, audience segmentation, offer variants, landing page scaffolding — and run rapid learning cycles.

  • Engineer the demand‑to‑pipeline path: ICP definitions, routing logic, handoff SLAs, and Sales feedback loops.

  • Identify new channels and build the playbook before you scale spend.

Growth Stack & Analytics

  • Instrument the growth funnel end‑to‑end across Salesforce, HubSpot, GA4, Webflow/CMS, and attribution/BI tooling.

  • Partner with RevOps and Analytics to establish taxonomy, data hygiene standards, experimentation frameworks, and attribution models that hold up under scrutiny.

  • Build dashboards and reporting infrastructure that make the "what's working" question answerable in real time — and translate results into insights, next actions, and investment guidance for Marketing and GTM leaders.

Cross-Functional Alignment

  • Serve as the DRI for growth: set strategy, run the operating cadence, and align Sales, RevOps, Product, and Brand around clear priorities and decision criteria.

  • Build influence without line authority — turn cross‑functional stakeholders into an integrated growth squad.

  • Maintain a transparent roadmap and experiment backlog; communicate trade‑offs and learnings frequently.

 

What You Have

  • Senior, hands‑on experience building integrated growth programs in B2B SaaS; healthtech experience a plus.

  • Demonstrated ownership of an MQL or pipeline number — you've been accountable for net new business outcomes, not just activity metrics.

  • Deep hands‑on experience building and optimizing ad engines across paid search, social, and programmatic; you know the platforms as well as the strategy.

  • Proven ability to take an early-stage marketing foundation and scale it into a high-output, repeatable growth system.

  • You're equally comfortable instrumenting a funnel as writing a high‑conversion brief — you've shipped real things in both modes.

  • Strong systems instinct: you design processes, taxonomies, and operating cadences that other people can actually use.

  • You influence without authority, move fast with incomplete information, and maintain high standards while doing it.

  • A bias toward building: when something doesn't exist, you make it.

 

Nice to Have

  • Built ABM motions in close partnership with Enterprise and Mid‑Market Sales.

  • Run product‑led and sales‑led motions in parallel.

  • Worked with data science on incrementality testing or advanced attribution.

  • Scaled a performance creative system across channels — briefing, asset libraries, structured testing.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Staff Product Designer to own design direction for a healthcare domain spanning multiple interacting workflows and product surfaces. You’ll turn ambiguous clinical and operational problems into a clear design agenda, shape product direction with business partners, and lead design from discovery through launch. Your work will connect individual features into holistic, coherent experiences for the people who deliver care and run medical practices.

This is a hands-on creative leadership role. You’ll set a clear creative direction for your domain, turning user insights and product strategy into compelling concepts, coherent interaction models, and a vision that helps teams see what’s possible. Through clear communication and mentorship, you’ll help experienced designers and cross-functional partners strengthen their design judgment.

Our design team operates like a studio: we critique work, share approaches, and develop our craft together. We use realistic prototypes and AI-assisted workflows to explore ideas and test assumptions, and clear writing to sharpen our thinking, explain design decisions, and articulate their value to users and the business. We partner closely with product, engineering, and operations to turn that understanding into better healthcare workflows.

Location and travel: This is a full-time role based at our headquarters in Mountain View, CA, with a minimum of 3 days per week in the office and occasional travel to client sites for field research and direct user engagement.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the design agenda for a domain. Bring structure to ambiguous problems, connect workflows across product surfaces, and identify the most important opportunities to improve user and business outcomes. Define success with your cross-functional partners and use evidence to assess progress.

  • Shape product direction and roadmaps. Synthesize user research, customer needs, business priorities, and technical constraints into a clear point of view. Partner with Product and Engineering to connect a longer-term experience vision to practical, sequenced investments.

  • Set and carry creative direction. Develop a strong point of view on how the product should work, look, and feel. Bring that direction to life through concepts, prototypes, and narratives, then guide the work through critique and implementation, raising the quality bar across teams while giving collaborators room to contribute.

  • Build deep understanding of users and their work. Lead research, including on-site observation and workflow testing, to understand clinical and practice operations. Map interactions across people, processes, and systems; uncover unmet needs and the root causes behind fragmented experiences.

  • Stay hands-on from concept through launch. Create clear interaction models, refined interfaces, and realistic prototypes. Validate ideas with users, address accessibility and edge cases, and work closely with engineers through implementation. Use feedback after launch to improve the experience.

  • Create durable patterns and shared approaches. Identify recurring problems across workflows and contribute reusable patterns, components, and abstractions to the design system. Help teams adopt approaches that improve coherence without ignoring meaningful differences in user needs.

  • Align people around clear decisions. Use design briefs, workflow maps, prototypes, and compelling narratives to explain opportunities and tradeoffs. Resolve competing priorities, coordinate dependencies across teams, and keep partners aligned through execution.

What You Have

  • A track record of domain-level ownership. You’ve led complex, end-to-end product design with impact across multiple workflows and teams. You can show how you helped define the problem, shaped direction, and stayed accountable through delivery and iteration.

  • Creative vision grounded in product judgment. You can move beyond incremental improvements to imagine better ways of working. Your portfolio shows how you established a direction, inspired others to build on it, and carried the strongest ideas into a shipped experience, including the tradeoffs you made and the outcomes of your work.

  • Exceptional interaction and visual craft. You simplify complex workflows without losing essential detail. Your work demonstrates strong information architecture, clear interaction models, thoughtful visual hierarchy, and attention to accessibility, edge cases, and error prevention.

  • Strong research, framing, and systems thinking. You turn incomplete information and conflicting requests into actionable insights and design opportunities. You build deep domain expertise and reason about how users, business operations, and technical systems interact.

  • Influence beyond your own execution. You’ve aligned cross-functional partners, mentored experienced designers, and improved the quality or effectiveness of work across teams. You can build trust, challenge assumptions constructively, and help others make sound decisions.

  • Clear writing and compelling storytelling. You can frame a problem in a design brief, articulate a domain-level vision, and explain decisions to design, technical, business, and customer audiences.

  • Applied experience with AI-assisted design and prototyping. You use tools such as Figma and AI-assisted development environments to explore concepts and build realistic prototypes, including code-based prototypes when appropriate. You can show how these workflows improved learning, quality, or speed, while protecting sensitive information and critically reviewing outputs. This expectation is about making ideas testable, not owning production engineering.

  • Ownership and sound judgment under ambiguity. You proactively identify work that matters, prioritize competing workstreams, communicate commitments, and balance speed with quality. You bring genuine curiosity about healthcare and the judgment to work in a high-trust environment.

What we offer

  • Meaningful ownership of complex healthcare problems, with influence over product direction and the opportunity to see your work through to real-world use.

  • A collaborative, studio-like design team that values critique, shared learning, and strong craft.

  • Opportunities to expand your impact through hands-on design, mentorship, and improvements that help multiple teams succeed.

  • Competitive compensation and benefits, with support for professional development and learning.

Please be aware that all official communication from us will come exclusively from email addresses ending in @commure.com. Any emails from other domains are not affiliated with our organization.

Employees will report to the information security office any confirmed or potential events or other risks to the organization. Employees will be required to attest to these requirements upon hire and on an annual basis.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

Commure builds AI for healthcare operations. Call Center Agents is our AI voice agent for medical practice and health system call centers. It answers and places patient calls, schedules and reschedules appointments, and plugs directly into the EHR, so calls end with work done rather than a message left.

We sell to health systems, specialty practices, FQHCs, and behavioral health networks. The product is moving fast, the market is crowded with well-funded competitors, and the team is small enough that one person can shape how the whole sales motion runs.

You'll be the person who makes the sales team measurably better every quarter. That means owning the numbers (pipeline, forecast, targets, rep performance) and the people side that moves them: coaching individual sellers and keeping the whole team sharp on a product that ships something new every few weeks.

You'll sit in deal reviews, tell us where the forecast is wrong before it's wrong, figure out why one rep converts discovery calls at twice the rate of another, and turn that into a training the rest of the team runs with the next week. If you've done sales strategy and ops at a high-growth company and want more scope, more ownership, and a mission in healthcare, this is that job.

What You'll Do

Set strategy and plan the business

  • Partner with the call center leadership on go-to-market strategy across segments: health systems, specialty practices, FQHCs, and behavioral health.

  • Lead territory design, target setting, and quota allocation. Translate company goals into field-level numbers each rep believes in.

  • Model capacity and hiring plans: how many reps, SEs, and implementation resources we need to hit the plan, and when.

  • Help design and administer sales comp, including SPIFs that push the behaviors we need.

Evaluate and improve individual sales performance

  • Build a performance scorecard for every seller: activity, pipeline generation, stage conversion, cycle time, win rate, and deal size.

  • Diagnose where each rep is losing deals (discovery, champion building, ROI case, procurement) using CRM data, call recordings, and deal reviews.

  • Run regular 1:1 performance reviews with reps and their managers. Agree on two or three specific things to improve and track whether they do.

  • Spot what top performers do differently and make it the playbook for everyone else.

Enable and train the team

  • Own sales enablement for Call Center Agents: onboarding for new hires and ongoing training for the existing team.

  • Run trainings whenever the product changes so every seller can demo, position, and price new capabilities the week they ship.

  • Build and maintain the core assets: pitch and demo scripts, discovery guides, objection handling, competitive battlecards, and ROI calculators.

  • Certify reps on the product and the pitch through role plays and mock calls, and retrain where the data shows gaps.

  • Be the link between Product and Sales: bring field feedback to the product team and bring product updates back to the field.

Build the systems

  • Own CRM hygiene, deal stage definitions, and KPI definitions so everyone reads the same numbers.

  • Build dashboards and reporting that reps, managers, and leadership actually use.

  • Move us from spreadsheets to scalable tools as we grow, and use AI tools to make the whole machine faster.

What You Have

  • 4+ years in sales strategy and operations, revenue operations, or GTM strategy at a high-growth tech company. Consulting, banking, or chief-of-staff experience before that is a plus.

  • You've run the core sales rhythm yourself: forecasting, pipeline reviews, business reviews, target setting, and territory or quota planning.

  • You've worked directly with sellers, not just their data. You can sit with a rep, look at their pipeline, and tell them specifically what to do differently.

  • You're comfortable in front of a room. You've built and delivered trainings, onboarding, or enablement programs that changed how a team sells.

  • Strong analytical skills: advanced Excel or Sheets, comfortable building models from scratch. SQL is a plus.

  • Hands-on with Salesforce or HubSpot, including reports and dashboards.

  • You bring structure to ambiguity with low ego. You'll build the deck, then clean up the CRM, then run the meeting.

  • Clear, concise writer and communicator with reps, managers, and executives alike.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Commure builds AI for healthcare operations. Call Center Agents is our AI voice agent for medical practice and health system call centers. It answers and places patient calls, schedules and reschedules appointments, and plugs directly into the EHR, so calls end with work done rather than a message left.

We sell to health systems, specialty practices, FQHCs, and behavioral health networks. The product is moving fast, the market is crowded with well-funded competitors, and the team is small enough that one person can shape how the whole sales motion runs.

You'll be the person who makes the sales team measurably better every quarter. That means owning the numbers (pipeline, forecast, targets, rep performance) and the people side that moves them: coaching individual sellers and keeping the whole team sharp on a product that ships something new every few weeks.

You'll sit in deal reviews, tell us where the forecast is wrong before it's wrong, figure out why one rep converts discovery calls at twice the rate of another, and turn that into a training the rest of the team runs with the next week. If you've done sales strategy and ops at a high-growth company and want more scope, more ownership, and a mission in healthcare, this is that job.

Set strategy and plan the business

 - Partner with the call center leadership on go-to-market strategy across segments: health systems, specialty practices, FQHCs, and behavioral health.

 - Lead territory design, target setting, and quota allocation. Translate company goals into field-level numbers each rep believes in.

 - Model capacity and hiring plans: how many reps, SEs, and implementation resources we need to hit the plan, and when.

 - Help design and administer sales comp, including SPIFs that push the behaviors we need.

Evaluate and improve individual sales performance

 - Build a performance scorecard for every seller: activity, pipeline generation, stage conversion, cycle time, win rate, and deal size.

 - Diagnose where each rep is losing deals (discovery, champion building, ROI case, procurement) using CRM data, call recordings, and deal reviews.

 - Run regular 1:1 performance reviews with reps and their managers. Agree on two or three specific things to improve and track whether they do.

 - Spot what top performers do differently and make it the playbook for everyone else.

Enable and train the team

 - Own sales enablement for Call Center Agents: onboarding for new hires and ongoing training for the existing team.

 - Run trainings whenever the product changes so every seller can demo, position, and price new capabilities the week they ship.

 - Build and maintain the core assets: pitch and demo scripts, discovery guides, objection handling, competitive battlecards, and ROI calculators.

 - Certify reps on the product and the pitch through role plays and mock calls, and retrain where the data shows gaps.

 - Be the link between Product and Sales: bring field feedback to the product team and bring product updates back to the field.

Build the systems

 - Own CRM hygiene, deal stage definitions, and KPI definitions so everyone reads the same numbers.

 - Build dashboards and reporting that reps, managers, and leadership actually use.

 - Move us from spreadsheets to scalable tools as we grow, and use AI tools to make the whole machine faster.


WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 4+ years in sales strategy and operations, revenue operations, or GTM strategy at a high-growth tech company. Consulting, banking, or chief-of-staff experience before that is a plus.

 - You've run the core sales rhythm yourself: forecasting, pipeline reviews, business reviews, target setting, and territory or quota planning.

 - You've worked directly with sellers, not just their data. You can sit with a rep, look at their pipeline, and tell them specifically what to do differently.

 - You're comfortable in front of a room. You've built and delivered trainings, onboarding, or enablement programs that changed how a team sells.

About the Role

At Commure, our Air AI team is building the intelligence layer that lives inside the clinical workflow — one that listens, documents, reasons, and acts so clinicians don't have to. The Provider Pod turns that intelligence into the daily clinician experience. The team works across AI-powered documentation that transcribes patient visits and structures them into clinical notes in real time, a conversational clinical assistant grounded in live patient context and medical literature, and an extensible AI Skills Library of reusable agents and workflows that automates clinical work across the platform. We also own the core provider surfaces around charting, clinical coding, treatments and flowsheets, orders, labs, prescriptions, and the signed encounter that powers downstream billing.

As the Engineering Manager for the Provider Pod, you'll lead a full-stack team responsible for building AI that clinicians trust with their most critical work. You'll own people leadership, technical direction, roadmap execution, and operational excellence across Python backend services, TypeScript/React product surfaces, and AI/LLM workflows. You'll partner closely with Product, Design, Clinical, AI/ML, Data, Platform, and RCM to turn ambitious ideas into intuitive, scalable, and reliable features that work in real clinical environments. This is a hands-on leadership role on a fast-moving team that celebrates large ambition, ships daily, and makes decisions quickly.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and grow the Provider Pod: Recruit, coach, and develop a high-performing team of full-stack engineers.

  • Own product and engineering outcomes: Drive the roadmap and execution across scribe documentation, the clinical assistant, reusable AI skills, and core provider workflows.

  • Set the technical direction: Guide architecture across Python services, TypeScript/React experiences, data systems, and AI/LLM workflows.

  • Partner cross-functionally: Work with Product, Design, clinical experts, AI/ML, Data, Platform, and Air Billing to ship intuitive solutions for real clinical environments.

  • Raise the engineering bar: Establish strong practices for planning, code quality, testing, deployment, and observability while keeping the team fast and pragmatic.

  • Drive operational excellence: Ensure provider-facing systems are reliable, secure, performant, and supported by effective on-call and incident response.

  • Build a high-ownership culture: Mentor technical leaders and foster strong judgment, customer empathy, healthy debate, and a bias toward action.

What You Have

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, required

  • 6+ years of software engineering experience, including 2+ years managing or formally leading engineers

  • Proven success hiring, coaching, and developing high-performing engineering teams

  • Strong full-stack technical depth across Python, TypeScript/React, APIs, data systems, containers, and cloud infrastructure

  • Hands-on experience integrating LLM APIs or shipping AI-powered features in production

  • Track record of driving complex, user-facing products from early ideation through successful production deployment

  • Strong product judgment, communication, and cross-functional leadership in fast-moving environments

  • Bonus: experience with EHRs, clinical software, healthcare interoperability, or regulated environments such as HIPAA and SOC 2

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We're hiring a Director, Finance Strategy & Operations to be the connective tissue of the finance organization and the DRI for the cross-functional programs that make finance work with the rest of the business. This is not a forecasting seat and not an accounting seat. It is a process, technology, and alignment seat: when we need to stand up quote-to-cash, build a customer data cube, redesign the planning calendar, or integrate an acquisition's finance stack, this is the person who owns the outcome, wrangles every team involved, and drives it to done. You’ll work directly with the most senior leaders of the company and drive the change that will enable this company to grow past $1B, helping a pre-IPO healthcare technology finance team that is building its infrastructure for scale. Critically, you'll also be a force multiplier for how finance adopts AI and LLM tooling in its own processes.

What You'll Do

  • Own Cross-Functional Finance Programs End-to-End: Serve as the directly responsible individual for multi-team initiatives spanning finance, revenue operations, engineering, legal, people, and product (e.g., quote-to-cash, customer and contract data cube, planning-to-close handoffs, M&A finance integration). Set scope, define success, sequence the work, and own the result.

  • Delegate Without Losing Accountability: Break programs into workstreams, assign them to the right owners across the org, run the cadence that keeps them moving, and personally unblock what stalls. You keep the whole picture even when you aren't doing every piece.

  • Build Strategic Alignment with the Business: Translate between finance and operators. Get sales, product, engineering, and corporate leaders to agree on definitions, owners, and timelines, and make sure finance processes reflect how the business actually runs rather than how finance wishes it ran.

  • Operate in a High-Visibility Seat: Your core stakeholders are the Head of FP&A, the Head of Finance, the Chief Legal & Corporate Officer, and the CEO. Expect to brief executives directly, frame the decisions they need to make, and be the face of finance on the programs you own.

  • Design Processes and the Systems Behind Them: Map current-state processes, design future state, and partner with Business Systems, Engineering, and vendors to implement. Own the finance-side requirements and acceptance for tools across the stack (NetSuite, Salesforce, planning platforms, data warehouse, internal tooling).

  • Take Any Project and Run With It: Act as the jack-of-all-trades the finance leadership team can hand an ambiguous, high-priority problem to with confidence that it will get structured, staffed, and finished.

  • Drive AI & Automation Into Finance Processes: Identify where LLM and automation tooling removes manual steps in the processes you own, pilot them, and institutionalize what works. Partner with the AI & Technology Finance lead on standards and governance.

  • Prepare the Finance Org for Scale: Document processes, controls, and ownership so that finance can grow toward IPO-readiness without linear headcount growth.

How You'll Spend Your Time

  • Day-to-day: Run program standups and workstream check-ins; unblock owners; draft requirements, decision memos, and process maps; field cross-functional questions that don't have an obvious home in finance.

  • Week-to-week: Steering meetings with program stakeholders; status and risk updates to finance leadership; alignment sessions with RevOps, Business Systems, Engineering, Legal, and People; review of in-flight system changes and their finance impact.

  • Month-to-month: Program milestone reviews; retrospectives on the close and forecast cycles with recommendations for process fixes; operating rhythm updates (calendar, OKR progress, decision log); AI/automation pilot reporting.

  • Quarterly & annual: Launch and land major programs; refresh the finance process and systems roadmap; coordinate the annual planning calendar across finance and the business; prepare finance-org readiness assessments (controls, documentation, audit, IPO).

Your Impact

  • Programs Actually Finish: Cross-functional finance initiatives that historically stalled between teams get a single owner and ship.

  • Finance and the Business Speak One Language: Shared definitions, owners, and timelines for the data and processes that connect the P&L to the operating reality (customers, contracts, sites, usage, headcount).

  • Leverage for Finance Leadership: The Head of Finance and Head of FP&A get back the hours they currently spend coordinating, and gain a trusted operator who can represent finance in any room.

  • Scalable Infrastructure: Process, systems, and governance that hold up through audit, diligence, and public-company readiness.

  • A More Automated Finance Org: Measurable reduction in manual steps across the processes you own, with AI and automation embedded where it earns its place.

What You'll Have

  • 8+ years across FP&A, strategic finance, business operations, finance transformation, consulting, and/or chief-of-staff roles, with a tour of duty in a high-growth, unstructured environment

  • A track record as the DRI on large cross-functional programs (e.g., quote-to-cash, ERP or planning-platform implementations, data warehouse or reporting builds, M&A integration) that you drove to completion through people who did not report to you

  • Strong process orientation: you instinctively map current state, define future state, assign owners, and set a cadence

  • Fluency across the finance stack and the business systems that feed it (NetSuite, Salesforce, planning platforms such as Pigment/Anaplan/Adaptive, data warehouses, internal tooling); comfort writing requirements and acceptance criteria for engineers and vendors

  • Enough finance and accounting literacy to understand what the close, the forecast, revenue recognition, and the board deck need from a process, without needing to own the numbers yourself

  • Hands-on LLM literacy (e.g., Claude Cowork & Code) and a point of view on applying AI to finance operations

  • Excellent written and verbal communication; able to run a steering meeting with VPs, write a one-page decision memo, and brief the CFO in two minutes

  • Low ego, high ownership; comfortable being accountable for outcomes you don't fully control

  • Familiarity with SQL and low/no-code dashboarding tools (e.g., Retool, Looker) is a plus

  • Experience in healthcare SaaS, pre-IPO environments, M&A integration, and/or program management certification (PMP, Lean/Six Sigma) is a plus

About the Role

We are looking for a driven and highly communicative Sales Development Representative (SDR) to join our growing Sales team in India.

As an SDR, you will be responsible for creating new sales opportunities by identifying and engaging potential customers, understanding their needs, introducing them to our solutions, and booking qualified product demonstration meetings for our Account Executives. This is a high impact, target driven role where your ability to communicate confidently, build relationships, learn quickly, and persist through challenges will directly contribute to our sales growth. You will work closely with our US based Sales organization and collaborate with Account Executives to ensure qualified prospects are successfully transitioned into the next stage of the sales process.

What You'll Do

  • Research and identify potential customers and relevant decision makers within target organizations

  • Proactively engage prospects through phone calls, email, LinkedIn, and other appropriate outreach channels

  • Communicate clearly and confidently with prospective customers in English

  • Understand prospects’ business needs, challenges, and interests to determine whether they are a good fit for our solutions

  • Clearly communicate the value of our products and create interest in learning more

  • Schedule qualified product demonstrations and sales meetings for Account Executives

  • Follow up consistently with prospects who have expressed interest but are not yet ready to engage

  • Maintain accurate and timely records of prospect interactions, follow ups, and meeting outcomes in relevant sales systems

If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We are seeking a Data Operations Analyst who will work at the intersection of QBR technical support and Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) data analysis. This role requires a strong mix of technical expertise (SQL, Excel, data validation), critical thinking, and attention to detail. The Analyst will be responsible for creating and enhancing QBR decks, running custom analyses, and ensuring high-quality data accuracy within patient verification and benefits processes.

The ideal candidate will bring strong analytical skills, a problem-solving mindset, and the ability to deliver error-free, business-critical outputs for internal teams and clients.

What You’ll Do

  • Deck Creation & Automation:

    • Run daily deck automations to generate reports (10–15%).

    • Own direct connect decks end-to-end: ensure 100% QA, escalate concerning metrics, and transition high-revenue decks to AMs (10–15%).

    • Work on custom and strategic QBR decks (30–40%), including adding tailored slides, insights, and SQL/Excel analysis that elevate reporting beyond standard decks.

  • Custom Analysis & Data QA

  • Client-Facing Custom Analysis: Support ad hoc requests from clients, including detailed SQL and Excel-based analysis, and develop custom Retool dashboards where applicable.

  • Data Verification: Validate that revenue transaction reports are accurately ingested from EHR systems and reconcile data discrepancies.

  • Quality Assurance Testing: Develop and execute test plans for data ingestion, identify discrepancies, and document QA results.

  • Mathematical/Financial Analysis: Apply quantitative reasoning to validate numerical accuracy in reports and ensure data integrity.

  • Process Improvement: Collaborate with engineering and operations teams to streamline QA processes, data workflows, and reporting accuracy.

  • Documentation & Reporting: Maintain records of QA activities, mappings, and findings, and present reports to stakeholders.

  • Compliance: Ensure all data handling complies with HIPAA and other regulatory requirements.

What You Have

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Mathematics, Healthcare Informatics, or related field.

  • Minimum 3 year of experience in data analysis, quality assurance, or technical reporting (healthcare/RCM preferred).

  • Strong technical ability: Proficiency in SQL and Excel (including pivot tables, VLOOKUP, macros, and data analysis).

  • Ability to perform quantitative reasoning to review metrics logically and identify inconsistencies.

  • High attention to detail – able to spot even the smallest errors before work is released.

  • Strong communication skills to relay insights, raise concerns, and collaborate across teams.

  • Familiarity with healthcare revenue cycle and financial reporting (preferred).

  • Experience with data visualisation tools (Tableau, Power BI) is a plus.

  • Growth mindset – ability to become semi-self-sufficient within 2–3 months.

  • Willingness to work in India Night Shifts (US Day shift – EST to PST).

Employees will be required to attest to these requirements upon hire and on an annual basis.

About the Role

We are hiring an Ambulatory AI Specialist to grow Commure's footprint with ambulatory organizations. You will own the full sales cycle for new-logo independent and specialty practices, multi-site medical groups, MSOs, and other outpatient organizations. Your work runs from prospecting and discovery through negotiation and close.

This is a full-portfolio role. You will lead with the product that solves a practice's most urgent problem, then expand into the rest of the Commure platform. You will not cover enterprise health systems. Your book is ambulatory.

What You'll Do

  • Build pipeline. Identify, prospect, and build pipeline within assigned ambulatory accounts. Use outbound outreach, events, referral partners, and EHR ecosystem relationships.

  • Run complex sales. Lead consultative discovery to uncover a practice's clinical, financial, and operational pain. Map those problems to the right mix of Commure products. Run the full sales cycle.

  • Expand accounts. Look for cross-sell and multi-product opportunities in every deal, and position the Commure platform rather than a single point solution.

  • Work as a team. Partner with solutions engineering, implementation, and customer success to ensure smooth handoffs and successful go-lives.

  • Keep forecasts accurate. Maintain accurate, current opportunity data in Salesforce. That includes stage, close date, ACV, product line, and forecast category. Deliver a reliable monthly and quarterly forecast.

  • Know the market. Stay current on the ambulatory market, competitors, and payer and reimbursement trends affecting outpatient practices.

  • Meet and exceed quota. Hit quarterly and annual targets for new-logo bookings.

What You Have

  • 5+ years of B2B sales experience, with 3+ years selling SaaS, AI, or tech-enabled services into ambulatory healthcare.

  • A track record of meeting or exceeding quota in a new-logo, full-cycle role.

  • Experience selling to both clinical and financial buyers, and building ROI cases that resonate with practice owners and CFOs.

  • Working knowledge of ambulatory workflows, the physician revenue cycle, and documentation challenges.

  • Familiarity with common ambulatory EHRs such as athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, ModMed, and Epic Community Connect.

  • Ability to sell a broad portfolio: learning multiple products, qualifying across them, and leading with the right one.

  • Strong discipline in Salesforce and pipeline management.

  • Self starter.

  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.

Nice to Have

  • Experience selling clinical workflow including, Ambient AI, Medical scribe solutions, remote patient monitoring, or RCM services

  • Existing relationships with medical groups, MSOs, or PE-backed physician platforms in [territory].

  • Experience selling into FQHCs or value-based care organizations.

  • Familiarity with MEDDICC or a similar sales methodology.

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
